title: Raise Your Triumphant Songs
description: Raise Your Triumphant Songs in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 104, headed “The same”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Raise your tri-um-phant songs To an im-mor-tal tune, Let the wide earth re-sound the deeds Ce-les-tial grace has done.

lines: Let the wide earth resound the deeds
And bid him raise our wretched race
No bolts to drive our guilty souls
When Christ was sent with pardons down
Bow to the sceptre of his love,
To the salvation thou hast brought,
And love and praise thy Name.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
